profile.campus: Hillsboro, Oregon (Flexential's Hillsboro data center campus, four existing buildings plus a fifth completed and a sixth planned as of 2025)

source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

profile.reading:
Per Flexential's own individual facility page, this building (Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 2) is located at 5737 NE Huffman St, Hillsboro, OR 97124. The operator publishes a footprint of 242683 square feet and 18 MW of critical load UPS capacity for this specific building, with published certifications and compliance attestations including PCI DSS, SOC 1 Type II, SOC 2 Type II, SOC 3, HITRUST, NIST 800-53, ITAR, SSAE 18. This building is part of Flexential's wider Hillsboro campus, which Data Center Dynamics reported in 2025 had grown to five sites (four existing buildings plus Hillsboro 5, then under construction) totaling 1.18 million square feet and 113 megawatts of capacity, with a sixth facility then being planned across from Hillsboro 1 at 350,000 square feet and 27 megawatts. Flexential president and COO Ryan Mallory described Hillsboro as "a smart alternative to Silicon Valley for customers seeking the performance, flexibility, and cost structure they can't find elsewhere, especially those with strong ties across the Pacific." DCD also reported that the Hillsboro market ran extremely tight in the first half of 2025, with a vacancy rate of just 0.2% and 48.4 megawatts of absorption against 48 megawatts of new supply delivered, roughly 10% of total market inventory turning over in six months. Hillsboro sits in Oregon's "Silicon Forest" technology corridor west of Portland, built up around Intel's long-standing local manufacturing presence and the skilled workforce it created, a legacy that has also drawn other major data center operators, including Meta, to the same area.

The City of Hillsboro reports that, as of July 2026, the city hosted 23 total data center sites, 16 already constructed across 346 acres plus 7 more in permitting or under construction across another 224 acres, together occupying roughly 570 of the city's 17,378 total acres. In 2025, Hillsboro's data center sector generated about $61.1 million in total taxes; 12 entities receiving Enterprise Zone property-tax abatements held roughly $7.2 billion in exempted real market value, out of an $11 billion combined assessed/exempted value across all data centers in the city. Eligible facilities receive temporary property-tax abatement on new investment for three to five years under Hillsboro's Enterprise Zone program, after which standard property taxes apply, alongside application fees capped at $50,000 and Community Service Fees of up to 33% of abated taxes in the first three years. Statewide, Oregon's data center industry supported an estimated 9,310 direct jobs and 38,380 indirect and induced jobs, with more than $4.1 billion in labor income, in 2023, according to industry analysis cited by the city.

reading.body:
Flexential Portland - Hillsboro 2 publishes 18 MW of IT capacity across 242,683 square feet of technical space. At 40 kW per rack, a common AI training density, 18 MW supports roughly 450 racks, and at 10 kW per rack, a common colocation density, the same power supports roughly 1,800 racks. The arithmetic is 18,000 kW divided by the assumed rack draw. Flexential has not published a per-rack power envelope for this facility, so neither figure is the operator's claim.

The certification stack qualifies this campus for a specific class of workloads. SOC 1 Type 2 and SOC 2 Type 2 address financial and operational controls auditing. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. ITAR qualifies it for defense-related technical data subject to export control. NIST 800-53 aligns it with federal security controls. HITRUST qualifies it for healthcare information. SSAE 18 is the auditing standard under which the SOC reports are issued. Together these certifications make the facility eligible to host regulated workloads that many general-purpose data centers cannot accept, though which tenants are actually present is not published.

Within Oregon, this site is the sixth-ranked campus by published IT capacity among only six facilities statewide that have published a megawatt figure at all, out of 133 mapped facilities total. The six published facilities sum to 182 MW, meaning Hillsboro 2 accounts for roughly 10 percent of that published total. Oregon's mapped facility count is large but its published-capacity base is thin, so 182 MW almost certainly understates the state's real installed capacity. This campus sits at the bottom of a short, incomplete list rather than at the edge of a well-characterized market.
